passage: This state of things continued until about 10 a. m., the enemy maintaining the attack
note: Ruger: at about 10 a.m. he orders two regiments (2d Mass., 27th Ind., Third Brigade, Colgrove) to try the enemy on the right of the breastworks, left of the swale (p.781); p.782: 'Lieutenant-Colonel Mudge, Second Massachusetts Volunteers ... who was killed while in command of his regiment, in the charge on the right on the forenoon of July 3.' Supported: event, units, Colgrove, ~10:00 anchor (the row's NPS value), forenoon. Not supported: 'near noon' (Wikipedia); 'fighting ended about 11:00'; strengths 650/1,000, 100 yd, 43%/32%; 'Mudge mortally wounded' (OR says killed, Ruger p.782, Colgrove R286 p.814 'fell'); the 'Spring' target. OR losses are Colgrove's 130 (2d Mass.) and 112 (27th Ind.) p.814.

passage: Jenkins' brigade, who here in the presence of the enemy allowed themselves to be supplied with but 10 rounds of ammunition
note: Stuart: on Jul 3 he moved to the left of Ewell's left with W. H. F. Lee's and Jenkins' brigades, Hampton's and Fitz. Not supported: 13:30-13:45 hour, 'withdraw after about 40 minutes', Union/Confederate totals (254/181/56), 3rd PA/1st NJ detail. Hampton wounded is in Stuart's list elsewhere (not re-read here). Conflict with T3-079 stays.
